unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of 49 CFR 392.10, the driver of a commercial motor vehicle specified in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of 49 CFR 392.10 must not cross a railroad track or tracks at grade unless he or she first stops the commercial motor vehicle within 50 feet of, and not closer than 15 feet to, the tracks, thereafter listens and looks in each direction along the tracks for an approaching train, and ascertains that no train is approaching.

unit_attributes.actor_quote: the driver of a commercial motor vehicle specified in paragraphs (a) (1) through (6) of this section
unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, for the driver of a commercial motor vehicle specified in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section crossing a railroad track or tracks at grade.
unit_attributes.modality_quote: shall not cross a railroad track or tracks at grade unless

unit_attributes.statement: When it is safe to do so, the driver of a commercial motor vehicle specified in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of 49 CFR 392.10 may drive the commercial motor vehicle across the tracks in a gear that permits the commercial motor vehicle to complete the crossing without a change of gears.
unit_attributes.scope_text: When it is safe to do so, for the driver of a commercial motor vehicle specified in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section driving across railroad tracks at grade.

unit_attributes.statement: The driver of a commercial motor vehicle specified in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of 49 CFR 392.10 must not shift gears while crossing the railroad tracks.
The commercial motor vehicles specified for the railroad crossing stopping rule include every bus transporting passengers.
The commercial motor vehicles specified for the railroad crossing stopping rule include every commercial motor vehicle transporting any quantity of a Division 2.3 chlorine.

The commercial motor vehicles specified for the railroad crossing stopping rule include every commercial motor vehicle which, in accordance with the regulations of the Department of Transportation, is required to be marked or placarded with one of the following classifications: Division 1.1; Division 1.2, or Division 1.3; Division 2.3 Poison gas; Division 4.3; Class 7; Class 3 Flammable; Division 5.1; Division 2.2; Division 2.3 Chlorine; Division 6.1 Poison; Division 2.2 Oxygen; Division 2.1; Class 3 Combustible liquid; Division 4.1; Division 5.1; Division 5.2; Class 8; or Division 1.4.

The commercial motor vehicles specified for the railroad crossing stopping rule include every cargo tank motor vehicle, whether loaded or empty, used for the transportation of any hazardous material as defined in the Hazardous Materials Regulations of the Department of Transportation, parts 107 through 180 of title 49.

The commercial motor vehicles specified for the railroad crossing stopping rule include every cargo tank motor vehicle transporting a commodity which at the time of loading has a temperature above its flashpoint as determined by 49 CFR 173.120.

The commercial motor vehicles specified for the railroad crossing stopping rule include every cargo tank motor vehicle, whether loaded or empty, transporting any commodity under exemption in accordance with the provisions of subpart B of part 107 of title 49.
A stop need not be made at a streetcar crossing, or railroad tracks used exclusively for industrial switching purposes, within a business district, as defined in 49 CFR 390.5.
A stop need not be made at a railroad grade crossing when a police officer or crossing flagman directs traffic to proceed.

A stop need not be made at a railroad grade crossing controlled by a functioning highway traffic signal transmitting a green indication which, under local law, permits the commercial motor vehicle to proceed across the railroad tracks without slowing or stopping.
A stop need not be made at an abandoned railroad grade crossing which is marked with a sign indicating that the rail line is abandoned.
A stop need not be made at an industrial or spur line railroad grade crossing marked with a sign reading “Exempt.”
Such “Exempt” signs marking an industrial or spur line railroad grade crossing shall be erected only by or with the consent of the appropriate State or local authority.
